title: Hero or Villain
description: Make moral choices under pressure and find out whether your instincts point toward Hero or Villain.

hero.label: Hero
hero.summary: Your choices lean toward protection, honesty, restraint, accountability, and helping people even when it costs you.

villain.label: Villain
villain.summary: Your choices lean toward control, ambition, leverage, punishment, and winning even when other people pay the price.

questions.prompt: You find a wallet full of cash and an ID. Nobody saw you pick it up. What do you do?

answers.text: Return it intact, even if nobody would know otherwise.
Return the ID but keep some cash as a finder fee.
Keep it all. Their bad luck is your opportunity.
Try to return it, but only after checking whether there is a reward.

questions.prompt: True or false: Power is only worth having if it helps protect people who have less of it.

answers.text: True
False

questions.prompt: A rival who humiliated you now needs your help. What is your first instinct?

answers.text: Help them because the emergency matters more than your pride.
Help them, but make it clear they owe you.
Refuse and let them learn what humiliation feels like.
Help only if it benefits people beyond the rival.

questions.prompt: You catch a friend cheating in a competition with real prizes. What do you do?

answers.text: Tell them to confess, and report it if they refuse.
Warn them privately and give them one chance to fix it.
Stay quiet because loyalty matters more than rules.
Use the secret later if you need leverage.

questions.prompt: True or false: Fear is an acceptable tool if it keeps people obedient.

answers.text: True
False

questions.prompt: A group is blaming one innocent person to calm a crowd. You know the truth. What do you do?

answers.text: Speak up immediately, even if the crowd turns on you.
Gather proof first so the truth cannot be dismissed.
Stay silent if exposing the truth makes life harder for you.
Trade the truth for a favor from whoever benefits most.

questions.prompt: You have a chance to take credit for someone else's work. Nobody can prove it was theirs. What happens?

answers.text: You credit them openly.
You share credit, even if you did less.
You take credit because recognition goes to whoever claims it.
You take credit now and privately reward them later.

questions.prompt: True or false: Mercy is weakness when someone has already lost.

answers.text: True
False

questions.prompt: A law is unfair but breaking it could get you punished. What guides you?

answers.text: Protecting people harmed by the law, even at personal risk.
Changing it carefully so fewer people get hurt.
Using the unfair law against enemies while you can.
Ignoring it only when it benefits you directly.

questions.prompt: You discover a secret that could ruin a powerful person who has hurt others. What do you do?

answers.text: Expose it responsibly with evidence and protect victims.
Use it to force them to stop harming people.
Blackmail them for personal gain.
Sell the secret to the highest bidder.

questions.prompt: True or false: If you caused harm, admitting it matters even when you could escape consequences.

answers.text: True
False

questions.prompt: A teammate makes a mistake that could cost the whole group. What do you do?

answers.text: Help fix it and take responsibility for improving the system.
Correct them firmly but without humiliating them.
Publicly shame them so nobody repeats it.
Let them fail so you look better by comparison.

questions.prompt: You can save one stranger or secure a major advantage for yourself. Which do you choose?

answers.text: Save the stranger without bargaining.
Save them, but only if it does not destroy your future.
Take the advantage. You did not create their danger.
Use their danger to negotiate an even better advantage.

questions.prompt: True or false: People deserve dignity even when they are weak, defeated, or unpopular.

answers.text: True
False

questions.prompt: A crowd offers you leadership after you solve a crisis. What kind of leader would you become?

answers.text: Transparent, accountable, and willing to step down if trust is lost.
Protective but firm, using authority only when needed.
Efficient and feared. Results matter more than consent.
Untouchable. If they gave you power, they can live with it.

questions.prompt: At the end of your story, what do you most want people to say about you?

answers.text: They made things better for people who needed help.
They had principles and stood by them under pressure.
They took what they wanted and nobody could stop them.
They were feared, remembered, and never ignored.
